reasoning_notes: I scored each candidate on four things, in roughly this priority. (1) Chain purity: do all of the entity's events sit as a subsequence of ONE causal chain? Candidates whose events straddle several unrelated chains (C-46, seven events spanning supply, auth, compliance, service and ops) were pushed to the bottom regardless of volume. (2) Causal ordering by first_seen_day: a genuine progression shows earlier chain positions appearing first. Strict inversions were treated as near-disqualifying (C-56 is chain D run backwards; C-44 has false_alarm before firmware_update; C-25 revenue_miss before yield_drop; C-1, C-13 workaround before policy; C-37 contract_penalty before sla_breach; C-0 audit_finding before data_exposure_risk). Skipped intermediate links were NOT penalised - a subsequence in correct order is still a chain. (3) Independent corroboration per link: I required most links to have independent_sources >= 2 spread over multiple sites and regions. Chains whose every link rests on a single report (C-5, C-51, C-3, C-35, C-23, C-31) were treated as background traffic even when ordered correctly. (4) Loud-site / echo check: I compared total_reports against independent_sources and distinct_sites. Where reports far exceed distinct reporters and cluster in one or two sites (C-59's manual_workaround: 22 reports, 4 sites, audit_finding confined to 1 site), I discounted; where high report counts came with many independent sources across 4+ sites and multiple regions (C-48, C-29), I did not. Length and breadth broke ties: longer in-order chains touching more regions ranked higher, and I gave partial credit to strongly-sourced two-link pairs (C-14, C-15, C-16, C-45) but kept them below the cut because two events are weak evidence of a progression. I marked 18 real - the ones that are single-chain, monotone in causal order, and multi-source at nearly every link. C-12 is the marginal inclusion (a complete five-step service-degradation chain in exact order, but three of its five links rest on one report each); C-17 and C-40 sit just at the boundary for the same reason.
